notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates. It also updates the SCCM Retro app for Horizon, on your SD card and for new downloads.

Game shortcuts: a game can have its own icon on the Horizon Home menu that starts SCCM Retro straight into that game. On the game's pre-launch menu, open Compatibility and choose Add a Home menu icon, then open the SCCM Retro app in Horizon and install it from Game shortcuts. The icon is the game's cover in an SCCM Retro frame. Icons need sigpatches or sys-patch, and on the system NAND the app shows a red warning and asks you to hold ZL and ZR first. A game started from its icon is no longer held up by the update offer.

Installing on more SD cards: an exFAT card is turned into FAT32 where it is, with every file kept; the app lists anything that would stop it first, such as a file over 4 GB. On a card with Android, SCCM Retro goes next to Android or takes its place, even when Android has no hekate entry (the installer checks the partitions before it erases anything). The app draws the card's partitions as a colored bar, so you can see what each choice keeps and what it erases.

Grow SCCM Retro gives a Linux partition that has run short of room more space, from the FAT32 side's free space or from Android's partitions. It runs on the charger and needs the internet.

Remove SCCM Retro: on a card whose Linux partition is already gone, Remove deletes only SCCM Retro's files and says that Android or your emuMMC stays as it is. A card with Android in front of SCCM Retro is refused with the reason, and nothing is changed.

GameCube and Wii: a setting made for one game now stays with that game. A CPU clock set for one game had been slowing every GameCube and Wii game played after it; this update clears that out. Pokemon XD starts at a 50 percent CPU clock, which holds a full 30 fps (it ran at about 24). Two-disc GameCube games change discs on their own.

One game at a time: starting a game while the last one is still closing waits for it, so two games never run at once. The menu's performance profile no longer carries over into a game.

Copy of settings and saves: the console keeps a copy of your settings and saves, with your BIOS files and keys, in the SCCM-Retro folder on the SD card. If Linux is ever removed and installed again, the copy is put back at the first start. Settings, Manage Files, Copy of settings and saves has Back up now and Restore.

Stream to OBS or VLC: Settings, Display and Sound streams the screen and sound to a PC on the same network, to record or restream from OBS or watch in VLC. The web page shows the address to open.

The web page's Files tab downloads to your computer: one file as it is, a folder or several items as a zip, protected files on the SD card included. MAME sets that are folders or loose files import too; they are zipped as they come in.

PC games get Render resolution (play at a lower resolution, scaled up to the screen), Sharpening, Frame limit and Controller: player 1 only rows.

Wind Waker HD: all of the game's own options are rows in its pre-launch menu, from invert and dead zone to gyro aiming, language, frame rate and resolution. A game built with an older release needs Rebuild on the web page before its frame rate, game speed, resolution and filtering rows take effect. Mario Kart Wii: a Wii NAND copied from a PC whose settings file stopped the game at "NAND initialization failed" is repaired before it starts.

The performance overlay has a refresh rate setting (every 1, 2 or 5 seconds) and shows the CPU clock the chip really runs. When a clock needs more voltage than Max voltage allows, the chip runs slower, and the overlay used to show the clock that was asked for. CPU Settings now shows the voltage ceiling in force, the chip's own when none is saved, and offers 1200 mV (1235 on Erista) as the default, what a fresh install sets. A Linux partition restored from another console now reads this console's chip.

Cover art: a weak match is no longer taken as a game's cover, and ports get art of their own instead of their base game's.

Tuning: a DDR200 test that fails says when the card switched and this console could not time it, and the console restarts into SCCM Retro after the test. Stall warnings no longer fire at startup, and a stall never restarts the console on its own. A custom RAM test with a timing at 0 runs that timing at stock. Erista consoles with MGCH memory get the community timing presets. The status page shows the voltages a session's tests run at, and a stuck audio service no longer holds a test.

New and lightly tested: turning an exFAT card into FAT32 and Grow have run on test card images and only a few real cards so far, so back up your SD card before either. Not tried yet: a stream into OBS or VLC (only the stream itself was checked, with no PC running either), Controller: player 1 only, and a real two-disc GameCube game.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
